title: 248 or 265 keV? Reconstructing the recoil energy of the LZ event with the tuned NEST model
question: What recoil energy follows from S1c=540.1 phd, S2c=9268 phd with the LZ-tuned NEST yields (S1, S2, combined, 2D likelihood), and how close is the event to the 269.9 keV efficiency edge and the S1c<600 phd cut?
headline_result: Table S5 as printed (nestpy 2.1.1) gives E_ML = 262 +- 11 keV (eff 0.71), but LZ's own energy contours and 269.9 keV efficiency edge imply Nq ~ 11.3 E^1.11 (+8% S1/keV), under which E_ML = 246 +- 10 (stat) +- 4 (g1) keV with eff 0.93; the paper's 248 keV is self-consistent and the event is on the efficiency plateau
key_numbers: E_S1 266.2 / E_comb 264.4 / E_ML 262.3 [251,273] keV (Table S5); E_ML 245.8 [236,255] keV (paper scale); contour crossings 298.8/418.8/543.8/671.1 phd; W_implied 13.46 eV; Nq offset +7.7% at 250 keV (beta=1.11 gives +5.7%); MC E50 291 vs 271.7 keV; eff(E_ML) 0.71 vs 0.93; P(S1c>600) 0.7%; band sigma 0.033 dex (MC) -> 1.46 sigma vs drawn 0.022 dex -> 2.5 sigma; g1 +-2% -> +-3.9 keV; delta_max 386.6 vs 389.9 keV; E_ee 69.7 keVee
model_or_mechanism: NEST v2 NR yields (Table S5 variants) + nestpy GetQuanta fluctuations + binomial/Fano detector model; digitised Fig. 2/4 contours; Fig. S2 roll-off
builds_on: LZ paper; dossier 00 (S2 checks i, ii)
agent_tools: Read x11, Bash x14, Write x5, Edit x11
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; nestpy 2.1.1; numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1; pandas 3.0.5; matplotlib 3.11.2; common/lzcommon.py
local_inputs: fulltext.tex (l.84-123, 590-690); Fig2/Fig4/FigS2 PNGs; dossier 00; dossier_numbers.json; lzcommon.py
recalled_knowledge: 3: W=13.7/13.5 eV (likely); NEST v2 NR yield functional form (likely); 10-90% = +-1.2816 sigma (certain)
